title: Clocking In the Right Way in Missouri CDS: The App, the Home Phone, and Fixing Mistakes
short_title: Clocking in the right way in CDS
description: Clocking in and out (EVV) is how Missouri CDS caregivers get paid. Here's how it works: the two ways to clock in, the habits that protect your pay, how to fix a missed clock-in with the EVV correction form (by 11:59 PM Saturday of that pay week), and why corrections are watched closely.
end: Clean clock-ins mean an on-time Thursday.

parts.head: Clocking in the right way
parts.sub: The app, the home phone, and fixing mistakes
parts.text: Clocking in and out is how you get paid as a CDS caregiver, so let's get it exactly right. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Here's how it works, the habits that protect your pay, and how to fix a mistake.

parts.head: The app, or the home phone
parts.sub: WellSky Personal Care app, or the consumer's home phone
parts.text: There are only two ways to clock in and out. One: the WellSky Personal Care app on your smartphone. Two: a call from the consumer's home phone, the number registered to their home.

parts.head: Not your own cell phone
parts.text: Calling from your own cell phone doesn't work, and isn't allowed. And there are no paper timesheets, ever.

parts.head: Whichever you'll do every time
parts.sub: App: quick. Home phone: no smartphone needed.
parts.text: Which one should you use? Whichever you'll do every time. The app is quick, and shows your hours as they add up. The home phone needs no smartphone, and works where the cell signal is poor.

parts.head: It isn't tracking you
parts.sub: Location only at clock-in and clock-out
parts.text: And the app isn't tracking you all day. It only confirms the location when you clock in, and when you clock out.

parts.head: Clock in first. Clock out right away.
parts.text: Now, the habits that protect your pay. Clock in before you start any work, not after. And clock out right when you finish, not later from the car.

parts.head: Check your times every day
parts.sub: Report real tasks. Keep your own record.
parts.text: Report the tasks you actually did. Check your recorded times every day, so a problem gets caught the same day. And keep your own simple record of your hours, just in case.

parts.head: The EVV correction form
parts.sub: You and the person you care for both sign
parts.text: Sometimes something really does go wrong: a dead phone, no signal, an app crash, or a clock-in you truly forgot. There's one right way to fix it: the correction form, online at our hub website. You and the person you care for both sign it.

parts.head: By 11:59 PM Saturday
parts.sub: Of that pay week. Save it to your home screen.
parts.text: Send it in by eleven fifty-nine P M on Saturday of that pay week. Save the form to your phone's home screen, so it's one tap away.

parts.head: Aim for 95% right the first time
parts.sub: Lots of corrections can lead to a review
parts.text: One caution. Our goal is ninety-five percent of visits clocked right the first time. Missouri Medicaid watches corrections closely, and a lot of them can lead to a review. So use the form when you really need it.

parts.head: Call us instead
parts.sub: We'll figure out what's going wrong
parts.text: If you're needing corrections most weeks, call us instead. We'll figure out what's going wrong, and fix it together.
Clean clock-ins mean an on-time payday, every Thursday. Questions? Call us at 417-218-2888. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS.
